seo.title: FAQ – HubGet
seo.description: Answers to common questions about HubGet: SmartScreen warnings, accounts, safety, admin rights and the EXE and MSI installers.
seo.ogDescription: Answers to common questions about HubGet: SmartScreen warnings, accounts, safety, admin rights and the EXE and MSI installers.

texty.t3: Edge says the installer “isn’t commonly downloaded”. What should I do?
texty.t4: Edge judges downloads by their reputation. A new installer that isn’t digitally signed yet and has been downloaded by only a few people doesn’t have any, so Edge warns – it doesn’t mean the file contains a virus. Only download HubGet from this website or from the [official releases on GitHub](@releases). In Edge, hover over the download and click **…** → **Keep** → **Show more** → **Keep anyway**. Windows SmartScreen may warn once more when you run it – see the next question. We’re preparing a free code signing certificate for open source (SignPath Foundation); with it, the warning should disappear over time.
texty.t5: Windows shows a SmartScreen warning when I run the installer. Is that okay?
texty.t6: The HubGet installer isn’t digitally signed yet, so Windows shows the “Windows protected your PC” dialog. Click **More info** and then **Run anyway**. A signed installer is on our roadmap.
texty.t8: HubGet is still in an early stage of development – the first public version 0.1.0 came out in October 2026 and updates have been arriving since (see [What’s new](changelog.html)). WinGet, Chocolatey, Scoop and developer package managers (npm, pip, Cargo and more) work for real – search, install, update and uninstall. You may run into the occasional bug.
texty.t10: Yes. HubGet is open source under the MIT license – free, with no ads and no bundled extras. The source code is on [GitHub](@github).
texty.t12: No. Signing in with GitHub is optional and only needed for ratings, reviews, adding screenshots and sync between computers. Installing, updating and uninstalling work without an account. The [privacy policy](privacy.html) describes what's stored when you sign in.
texty.t13: Where does HubGet download apps from? Is it safe?
texty.t14: Only from the official repositories of package managers. HubGet downloads the installer and WinGet verifies its SHA-256 checksum before running it – if the file differs from the published one, the installation doesn’t happen.
texty.t15: Will HubGet show apps I installed before?
texty.t16: Yes. The installed apps overview includes programs installed outside WinGet, Microsoft Store apps and Steam games. You can update them, uninstall them or launch them with the Open button.
texty.t18: Not to install HubGet – the EXE installer installs for the current user. If installing an app requires administrator rights, HubGet retries it and asks for them (UAC).
texty.t19: What’s the difference between the EXE and MSI installers?
texty.t20: The EXE is recommended for most people: it installs without administrator rights and offers English and Czech. The MSI is meant for deploying across a company.
texty.t21: Didn’t find an answer? [Write to us](contact.html).
